claims.claim: Origin bootstrap requires a trusted in-document Human click, a 256-bit challenge expiring after 30 seconds, and proof through a private document handle. Copied tokens, page-created APIs, focus, recent chats, and repository identity cannot establish origin.

The conversation-keyed registry reuses stable opaque handles, rejects collisions, and serializes competing bindings. Deterministic tests assert repeated, distinct, same-conversation-tab, and reload route behavior. Handles confer no lifecycle authority.

Raw conversation identity and browser endpoint bindings remain in a bounded external registry that rejects working-tree and bare-repository locations. Bootstrap outputs contain fixed status fields and opaque metadata; confidentiality tests assert raw identity exclusion.

Bootstrap orders exact-page proof, durable binding, revalidation, proved draft-preserving insertion, durable attempt marking, and submission. Deterministic tests assert fail-closed page, challenge, surface, write, registry, generation, and insertion failures, plus blocking after ambiguous attempts.

One bounded development script attaches to an existing authorized loopback browser environment and exposes the in-page Human gesture. It requires no Developer Mode, MCP, Responses API, ChatGPT Work, or session metadata.

The implementation adds origin capture without H4C1 routing, wake delivery, lifecycle authority, or a wake queue. Existing local-chat-wake code and tests remain unchanged; bootstrap tests prohibit invoking wake delivery and canonical freshness operations.

H4C0 documentation defines the post-publication A1/A2 and B1/B2 comparisons, same-repository distinction, reload/reopen continuity, ambiguity rejection, confidentiality, and Human/Brain closure decision. TASK-293 acceptance and publication alone neither close H4C0 nor authorize H4C1.
